You're working in a Next.js 16 + Tailwind v4 app at /Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/web (product: Earshot, live AI captions for YouTube videos; dark theme, amber accent `accent`, red `live`, ink-* greys defined in packages/shared/src/theme.css; there's a global `mark.earshot-hit` highlight style there too).

The home page hero has a fake product demo on the right, in src/components/hero-demo/. All pieces share one simulated session from src/components/hero-demo/state.tsx (read it first: `useHeroDemo()` gives time, heard (indices into SCRIPT captured so far), current, query/setQuery, seek, showTranscript, etc.; also SCRIPT and formatTime). It's a scripted talk on a clock; no real audio.

YOUR JOB: make src/components/hero-demo/TranscriptCard.tsx interactive and driven by that state. Edit ONLY that file. Other agents are editing VideoFrame.tsx, ExtensionPopup.tsx and PlayerControls.tsx in parallel and I'm editing HeroDemo.tsx and page.tsx; don't touch those or state.tsx. If you need something from state.tsx, tell me in your report instead of changing it.

What it should do (mirrors the real transcript in the app: src/components/WatchExperience.tsx and related files are worth a quick look for how the real one behaves and is labelled):
- Replace the hardcoded TRANSCRIPT with lines from `heard` (SCRIPT[i]), timestamps via formatTime. The line equal to `current` is highlighted (existing amber style: bg-accent/10, amber timestamp). New lines appear as they're heard (subtle fade/slide-in, none under prefers-reduced-motion).
- The list has a fixed max height that fits the current card size (it shows about 3 lines now; keep the card roughly the same height, ~3 to 3.5 lines visible) and scrolls internally, auto-scrolling to keep the current/latest line in view, but NOT scrolling the page (use scrollTop on the list element, not scrollIntoView). Use the `earshot-scroll` class for thin scrollbars.
- Each line is a button: click seeks the player to that line's time (`seek(line.t)`), keyboard accessible, visible focus, hover state.
- The search box becomes a real input bound to query/setQuery (placeholder "Search the transcript", aria-label). Matching text is highlighted with `<mark className="earshot-hit">`; non-matching lines are hidden while a query is set; show a short empty message like "No matches" when none. The round button on the right clears the search when there's a query (aria-label "Clear search", x icon) and otherwise focuses the input (search icon).
- "Download" in the header: make it a button that downloads a .txt of the heard lines ("0:12 Good morning…" per line) via a Blob + temporary object URL, filename like "earshot-transcript.txt". 
- Before anything is heard (heard empty), show a muted line like "Lines appear here as they're spoken."
- Keep the existing look (rounded-[20px] bg-ink-900 card, ring, shadow, font sizes). Width is set by the parent; don't set your own.

Code style: TypeScript strict (noUncheckedIndexedAccess is on), "use client" stays, Tailwind, no new deps, no em dashes in visible text. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` from apps/web. Do NOT start or restart a dev server (one is running on 127.0.0.1:3100; I'll check visually). Report: what you changed, anything you wanted from state.tsx.

content.text:
I rewrote `apps/web/src/components/hero-demo/TranscriptCard.tsx` (the only file I touched) so it runs off `useHeroDemo()`. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passes with no errors. I didn't start the dev server or look at it in a browser, so the visual check is still yours.

- **Lines:** each heard line shows its `formatTime` timestamp and text. The `current` line gets the existing amber style and `aria-current`. New lines fade and slide in through Tailwind's `starting:` variant, and there's no motion under prefers-reduced-motion. The list is a `role="log"` region labelled "Transcript", like the real `TranscriptView`.
- **Height and scroll:** the list has a fixed `h-[6.5rem]` (about 3.3 single-line rows, so the card stays about the size it was) with `earshot-scroll` and `overscroll-contain`. When the current or latest line changes it adjusts the list's own scroll position, smoothly unless reduced motion is on, so the page never scrolls. While a search is active it stops auto-scrolling so it doesn't fight the user.
- **Seek:** each line is a full-width button that calls `seek(line.t)`. It has a "Jump to m:ss" tooltip, a hover state and an amber focus outline drawn inside the edge so the scroll area doesn't clip it.
- **Search:** the input is bound to `query`/`setQuery`, with the placeholder and aria-label "Search the transcript". Matching is case-insensitive and ignores leading and trailing spaces. Matches are wrapped in `<mark className="earshot-hit">` using the same highlight logic as `TranscriptView`. Lines that don't match are hidden, and "No matches" shows when nothing matches. Escape clears the search. The right-hand button shows an x labelled "Clear search" when there's a query, and a search icon that focuses the input when there isn't.
- **Download:** a button that saves `earshot-transcript.txt` with one "0:12 Good morning…" line per heard line, using a Blob and an object URL that's released afterwards. It's disabled while nothing has been heard.
- **Empty state:** when `heard` is empty it shows "Lines appear here as they're spoken." This also appears after the clock loops back and clears the lines, until the first line comes round again at 0:12.

Two behaviours you'll see when checking it. The lines already heard when the page loads fade in once on first render. Lines that come back when you clear a search animate in again.

I didn't need anything changed in `state.tsx`.
